CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty swallowing with chest pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Raymond is a patient presenting with several weeks of dysphagia and associated chest pain with swallowing. Pain occurs when swallowing most foods, particularly larger pieces that feel stuck. Patient denies weight loss but reports weight gain over the past month. Reports occasional epigastric pain. Symptoms appear to have been exacerbated by recent stress related to relocation from west coast to east coast over the last couple of months, during which time patient has been consuming less healthy foods including pizza and burgers, and reports increased alcohol consumption.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Denies hematochezia or melena. No fever reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is relocating from west coast to east coast and describes the move as stressful. Has a dog and is concerned about travel arrangements; plans to drive. Reports increased consumption of pizza, burgers, and alcohol due to stress.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: BP 133/70, HR normal, no fever, O2 saturation 100%, RR 19. Weight gain of approximately 10 pounds over the past month noted. HEENT: No ulcers or thrush. Tonsils midline. Neck: No adenopathy, no thyromegaly. Abdomen: Nondistended with active bowel sounds. Epigastric palpation negative for pain. Negative Murphy's sign, negative peritoneal signs, no rebound tenderness. Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Skin: No rash, lesion, or bruising. Eyes: Equal and reactive to light.

RESULTS
Barium swallow showed two areas of mild narrowing in the mid and lower portions of the esophagus consistent with esophagitis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Acute esophagitis. Started Protonix 40 mg once daily in the morning and Carafate 1 gram four times daily for one month. Scheduled for upper endoscopy. Patient counseled to decrease alcohol and caffeine consumption, avoid citrus fruits and spicy foods, eat slowly, and chew food more thoroughly. Follow-up appointment scheduled for next week for endoscopy procedure.
